title: Biodiversity and Ecosystems
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Biodiversity and Ecosystems Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Living things are diverse, can be grouped, and interact in their ecosystems: biodiversity in the local environment, characteristics of local plants, animals and fungi, populations and communities, and First Peoples knowledge of the local environment. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 3, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets (BC): biodiversity, grouping living things, habitats, populations and communities, and living things in soil. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Biodiversity is the variety of living things in a place.
key_sub: A population is one kind of living thing; a community is all of them together.
body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem is all the living and non-living things in an area working together: plants, animals and fungi, plus water, soil, air and sunlight. Biodiversity is how many different kinds of living things are there. A population is all the members of one species in an area; a community is all the populations living together.

Scientists group living things by their features. Fungi such as mushrooms are not plants: they cannot make their own food and get it from dead material. Caring for the local environment is a shared responsibility (stewardship).

Example

All the deer in a forest are a…

One kind of animal in one place

Answer: population

Example

Is a mushroom a plant?

Does it make food from sunlight?

Answer: no, it is a fungus

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up population (one species) and community (many species).
  • Calling fungi plants.
  • Forgetting non-living parts (water, soil, sunlight) of an ecosystem.

faq.a: Many kinds of living things make an ecosystem stronger and better able to recover from change.
Taking care of the environment so it stays healthy for everyone.

items.q: What does a habitat give an animal?
items.e: Its basic needs.

items.q: A loon needs clean lakes with fish. What would happen if the lake became polluted?
c: The loon would start eating plants.
The loon might not find enough food and might leave or die.
items.e: Habitats must meet an animal's needs.

items.q: Which of these lives in the ocean: a newt, a pond snail, a whale or an Arctic fox?
items.e: Each habitat has its own plants and animals.

items.q: Why can a fish not live in a forest?
c: A fish needs water to breathe and move.
items.e: Each living thing is suited to its habitat.

items.q: What is a habitat?
c: the place where a plant or animal lives and gets what it needs
items.e: A habitat gives food, water, shelter and space.

items.q: Which of these lives in the Antarctic: a duck, a penguin, a starfish or an oak tree?
items.e: Each habitat has its own plants and animals.

items.q: Which habitat does a scorpion live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: How do the features of a duck help it in its habitat? It has webbed feet and waterproof feathers.
c: They help it swim and stay dry in a pond.
They help it hunt in the dark woods at night.
They help it breathe and swim under water.
They help it stay safe when waves bash it on the rocks.
items.e: Animals are suited to their habitats.

items.q: What is a population?
c: all the members of one kind of living thing in an area
all the different animals in a forest
items.e: For example, all the white-tailed deer in a park.

items.q: Which habitat is very cold and icy?
items.e: Near the North Pole.

items.q: Which habitat does a whale live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: Which is a non-living part of a forest habitat?
items.e: Rocks, water, air and sunlight are non-living.

items.q: Which habitat does a crab live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: What do all animals need from their habitat?
items.e: These are the needs of animals.

items.q: How do the features of a penguin help it in its habitat? It has a thick layer of fat and short, tight feathers.
c: They help it jump and swim in and around a pond.
They help it live where it hardly rains.
They help it climb trees and balance on branches.
They help it keep warm in icy seas.
items.e: Animals are suited to their habitats.

items.q: Which habitat does an owl live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: What is a community?
c: only the plants in a forest
the soil and rocks in a place
all the plants and animals that live together in one habitat
items.e: A community includes all the living things in a habitat.

items.q: Which animal would you find in a rock pool at the seashore?
items.e: Rock pools are seashore homes.

items.q: How do the features of a frog help it in its habitat? It has long back legs and webbed feet.
c: They help it breathe and swim under water.
They help it jump and swim in and around a pond.
They help it climb trees and balance on branches.
They help it walk on sand and go a long time without food.
items.e: Animals are suited to their habitats.

items.q: Which living thing has features that help it jump and swim in and around a pond?
items.e: A frog has long back legs and webbed feet.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find an ant?
c: under a log or a stone
in a nest under a patio stone
items.e: Small creatures live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: What is it usually like on a sunny path?
items.e: Microhabitats each have their own conditions.

items.q: Which word best describes all the different plants and animals living on the rocky shore?
items.e: A community is all the populations living together in a habitat.

items.q: Which word best describes the pond itself, where the living things are found?
items.e: A habitat is the place where organisms live.

items.q: What is it usually like in leaf litter?
items.e: Microhabitats each have their own conditions.

items.q: All the Canada geese in one wetland are a …
items.e: One kind of animal in one place is a population.

items.q: Would you find many sow bugs in the soil?
c: No, sow bugs dry out in bright, warm places.
Sow bugs live only in ponds.
Yes, they like dark, damp places.
Sow bugs live only in trees.
items.e: Sow bugs need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Would you find many sow bugs on top of a wall in the sun?
c: No, sow bugs dry out in bright, warm places.
Sow bugs live only in ponds.
Yes, they like dark, damp places.
Sow bugs live only in trees.
items.e: Sow bugs need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Which is a living part of a pond?
items.e: Algae are living things.

items.q: Which word means 'a living thing'?
items.e: Plants, animals and fungi are organisms.

items.q: What is it usually like in the soil?
items.e: Microhabitats each have their own conditions.

items.q: A raccoon, a maple tree and some worms all live in the same park. What is this group called?
items.e: Different living things in one place make a community.

items.q: What is it usually like under a log?
items.e: Microhabitats each have their own conditions.

items.q: Which pair are both non-living parts of a habitat?
items.e: Living things grow and reproduce; water and sunlight do not.

items.q: Which word best describes all the mynahs living in the school field?
items.e: A population is one kind of organism in a habitat at the same time.

items.q: Would you find many sow bugs under a log?
c: Yes, they like dark, damp places.
Sow bugs live only in ponds.
Sow bugs live only in trees.
No, sow bugs dry out in bright, warm places.
items.e: Sow bugs need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Which word best describes one centipede in the rotting log?
items.e: One living thing is an organism, not a population.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find a ladybug?
c: under a log or a stone
in a nest under a patio stone
on the leaves of a plant
items.e: Small creatures live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: Would you find many sow bugs on a sunny path?
c: Sow bugs live only in trees.
No, sow bugs dry out in bright, warm places.
Sow bugs live only in ponds.
Yes, they like dark, damp places.
items.e: Sow bugs need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find a beetle?
c: in a nest under a patio stone
in a web in a hedge
items.e: Small creatures live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: A rotting log is home to millipedes, ants and mushrooms. What is the rotting log?
items.e: It is the place where they live.

items.q: What is a population?
c: all the animals in a habitat
a group of one kind of organism living in a habitat at the same time
all the plants and animals in a habitat
items.e: All the guppies in a pond form a population.

items.q:
OrganismNumber counted
Water lilies30
Frogs1
Guppies14
Hydrilla plants37
Snails10
Dragonflies13
Ethan counted the organisms in a pond. How many organisms are there in this community altogether?
items.e: Add the numbers of all the populations: 105.

items.q: Which statement about a habitat is correct?
c: A habitat provides food, water, shelter and air for organisms.
Organisms do not need a habitat.
A habitat has only one kind of organism.
A habitat is always very large.
items.e: Habitats can be big (a forest) or small (a rotting log).

items.q: Which of these is a population in the school field?
c: the water and soil of the school field
one butterfly in the school field
all the butterflies and mynahs in the school field
all the butterflies in the school field
items.e: A population is made up of one kind of organism only.

items.q: Which of these is a community in the rotting log?
c: the rotting log and the air above it
all the centipedes in the rotting log
all the plants and animals living in the rotting log
only the animals in the rotting log
items.e: A community has all the populations: plants and animals together.

items.q:
OrganismNumber counted
Love grass plants23
Mynahs7
Butterflies31
Earthworms11
Grasshoppers34
Ants12
Priya counted the organisms in a school field. How many populations did Priya record?
items.e: Each kind of organism is one population, so there are 6.

items.q:
OrganismNumber counted
Barnacles20
Limpets35
Seaweed plants36
Sea anemones29
Noah counted the organisms on a rocky shore. How many organisms make up the population of seaweed plants?
items.e: The population of seaweed plants is all the seaweed plants: 36.

items.q: Which of these is a community in the school field?
c: only the animals in the school field
the school field and the air above it
all the plants and animals living in the school field
all the love grass plants in the school field
items.e: A community has all the populations: plants and animals together.

items.q: Which of these is a community in the pond?
c: all the plants and animals living in the pond
only the animals in the pond
all the water lilies in the pond
the pond and the air above it
items.e: A community has all the populations: plants and animals together.

items.q: Water plants such as Hydrilla help fish in a pond. How?
c: They give out oxygen when they make food in light.
items.e: Fish need oxygen dissolved in the water.

items.q: Which of these is a population in the rotting log?
c: all the centipedes and mushrooms in the rotting log
all the centipedes in the rotting log
one centipede in the rotting log
the water and soil of the rotting log
items.e: A population is made up of one kind of organism only.

items.q: A beaver builds a lodge in a pond. What need does the lodge meet?
items.e: The lodge keeps the beaver safe and warm.

items.q: Organisms in a community depend on each other. Which is an example?
c: Bees get nectar from flowers and help to pollinate them.
A rock gives shelter to a fish.
items.e: Both organisms are living.

items.q: Which environmental factors affect where organisms live?
c: only the size of the animals
only the colour of the soil
items.e: These are called physical factors.

items.q: Earthworms come up to the surface of a field after heavy rain. Which factor has changed?
c: amount of water in the soil
items.e: The soil is full of water, so they come up.

items.q:
OrganismNumber counted
Earthworms16
Millipedes27
Mushrooms36
Leah counted the organisms in a rotting log. How many populations did Leah record?
items.e: Each kind of organism is one population, so there are 3.

items.q: Why do the barnacles on a rocky shore close up at low tide?
c: to keep in water so they do not dry out
items.e: At low tide they are out of the water.

items.q: Which of these is a community on the rocky shore?
c: the rocky shore and the air above it
all the plants and animals living on the rocky shore
all the crabs on the rocky shore
only the animals on the rocky shore
items.e: A community has all the populations: plants and animals together.

items.q: Ferns grow well under tall trees in a forest. Which factor most likely helps them grow there?
items.e: Many ferns grow well in shady, damp places.

items.q: Which group does a seal belong to?
items.e: Seals have fur, breathe air and feed their young on milk.

items.q: Which group does a crab belong to?
items.e: A crab is a crustacean.

items.q: Which group of living things does bread mold belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
c: to group them by shared features so they are easier to study
items.e: Classification shows how living things are related.

items.q: Which group does a bee belong to?
items.e: A bee is an insect.

items.q: Which group of living things does a moss belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group of living things does an ant belong to?
items.e: Animals feed on other living things and most can move from place to place.

items.q: An animal has fins and scales and takes oxygen from water with gills. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of fish.

items.q: A spring peeper lives in water as a tadpole and on land as an adult. Which group is it in?
items.e: Amphibians change from water to land.

items.q: An animal has six legs and three body parts. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of insects.

items.q: A dichotomous key gives two choices at each step. What do you do?
c: pick the choice that matches the living thing and follow it
items.e: Each step splits the group in two.

items.q: What is a species?
c: a group of living things that can breed and have young that can also breed
items.e: Moose are one species.

items.q: Which feature do all insects share?
c: six legs and three body parts
items.e: Spiders have eight legs, so they are not insects.

items.q: Which group does a newt belong to?
items.e: A newt is an amphibian.

items.q: Which group does a slug belong to?
items.e: A slug is a mollusc.

items.q: An animal lives in water, breathes with gills and has scales and fins. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of fish.

items.q: Which group does a snake belong to?
items.e: A snake is a reptile.

items.q: Which group does a mussel belong to?
items.e: A mussel is a mollusc.

items.q: An animal has a head, thorax and abdomen and six jointed legs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of insects.

items.q: An animal has a hard outer skeleton, two pairs of antennae and lots of legs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of crustaceans.

items.q: What is soil made of?
c: tiny bits of rock, humus (rotting plants and animals), air, water and living things
items.e: Soil is a mixture.

items.q: What do earthworms leave behind that is good for plants?
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: What is humus?
c: the dark part of soil made from decaying plants and animals
items.e: Humus gives soil nutrients.

items.q: What is composting?
c: turning food scraps and leaves into rich soil with the help of decomposers
items.e: Compost feeds plants.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Bacteria break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
c: Rocks are made of one or more minerals.
items.e: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica.

items.q: What do earthworms eat?
c: dead leaves and plant material in the soil
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: Where do earthworms like to live?
c: in dry sand in the sun
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: Which soil holds the most water?
items.e: Clay has tiny grains packed close together.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Mushrooms break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: What is soil made of?
c: tiny bits of rock, humus, water, air and living things
items.e: Soil is a mixture.

items.q: How can you test how hard a rock is?
c: Try to scratch it with a fingernail, a coin and a steel nail.
items.e: Harder rocks are harder to scratch.

items.q: Why is soil important to people?
c: We grow food in it and it filters water.
items.e: Healthy soil is a resource.

items.q: What happens to dead leaves on the ground over time?
c: They rot and become humus in the soil.
They stay the same for ever.
They grow back on the tree.
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: Which living things break down dead leaves into soil?
c: decomposers like worms, fungi and bacteria
items.e: Decomposers recycle nutrients.

items.q: Which soil feels sticky when wet?
items.e: Clay is smooth and sticky.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: Which kind of soil is best for growing most garden plants?
c: loam (a mix of sand, silt, clay and humus)
items.e: Loam holds water and drains well.

items.q: Many Indigenous peoples see soil as part of Mother Earth. What does this teach?
c: to use up the soil quickly
to care for the land and give back to it
items.e: Respect for the land helps protect soil.

items.q: Which animal lives in soil?
items.e: Many small animals live underground.
